_verificationNote.whyNotIndexed: IRC 224 (added by P.L. 119-21 sec. 70201) contains no inflation-adjustment clause. Rev. Proc. 2025-32 (the 2026 inflation adjustments) has NO section for IRC 224, confirming the $25,000 cap and the $150,000/$300,000 thresholds are the same fixed statutory figures for tax years 2025 through 2028.
_verificationNote.sunset: No deduction for any taxable year beginning after 2028-12-31 (IRC 224(h)). This file must not be cloned forward past tax year 2028.
howToRecheckAnnually: 1. Schedule 1-A (Form 1040), Part II — the authoritative computation, including the rounding convention: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/f1040s1a.pdf
2. Instructions for Schedule 1-A, inside the Form 1040 instructions: https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i1040gi.pdf
3. The year's IRS inflation-adjustment revenue procedure — check whether an IRC 224 section has appeared (it had not as of Rev. Proc. 2025-32): https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf
_verificationNote.roundingIsDeliberatelyDifferent: phaseOut.fractionCountsAsFullStep is FALSE here, and that is correct. Schedule 1-A line 11: 'Divide line 10 by $1,000. If the resulting number isn't a whole number, DECREASE the result to the next LOWER whole number. (For example, decrease 1.5 to 1, and decrease 0.05 to 0.)' IRC 224(b)(2)(A) says 'for each $1,000' with NO 'or portion thereof'. This is the OPPOSITE of car-loan.2026.json, where IRC 163(h)(4)(C)(ii)(I) does say 'or portion thereof' and Schedule 1-A line 28 rounds UP. The three flags must never be 'harmonised'.
_verificationNote.fixedOn: 2026-08-15 — fractionCountsAsFullStep flipped true → false, and the false branch of phase-out.ts changed from roundHalfUpToCent to Math.floor. Both changes were required: half-up rounding is not floor.
